name: Numerological Evocation — Additional Material (d20pfsrd)
body:
More on Numerological Evocation from d20pfsrd.com.

These sections appear on d20pfsrd.com's pages "Numerological Evocation", "Numerological Evocation" but are not part of the Numerological Evocation entry, which is unchanged.

From d20pfsrd.com: Numerological Evocation

CASTING

Casting Time 1 standard action
Components V, S

EFFECT

Range see text
Target see text
Duration instantaneous
Saving Throw Reflex half; Spell Resistance yes

DESCRIPTION

The Path of Numbers

The Path of Numbers is a system of numerology that describes eight basic energies. Any of these types of energy can interact at any time, producing 64 possible combinations. It is believed that those 64 combinations are sufficient to describe the basis of every interaction in the cosmos. No matter the plane, creature, or time in question, every event in the multiverse is based on one of those 64 templates. In short, the Path of Numbers is a periodic table of energetic elements.

From d20pfsrd.com: Numerological Evocation

CASTING

Range see text
Target see text
Duration instantaneous
Saving Throw Reflex half; Spell Resistance yes

DESCRIPTION

This was made to be a better version of this spell, because imo the wording is bad and confusing. And forums seem to agree.

Table: Eight Basic Energies
d8	Element	Magic School	Target	d20 Roll
1	Air	Enchantment	Touch	Will saves
2	Electricity	Illusion	Ray (single target)	Reflex saves
3	Fire	Necromancy	Ray (one ray per 3 levels, max 3)	Attack rolls
4	Sonic	Evocation	30 foot cone	Initiative rolls
5	Acid	Abjuration	60 foot line	Fortitude saves
6	Water	Transmutation	10 foot square burst	Caster level checks
7	Cold	Divination	20 foot radius spread	Concentration checks
8	Earth	Conjuration	One wall; 20 ft. high, 20 ft. long	Combat Maneuver Checks

You can use the Path of Numbers to calculate the latent magical energies all around you and create effects which vary depending on what is rolled. Roll 1d8 for each of the sections of the table above.

Element modifies what the ‘core element’ of the spell is, the Magic School is what the spell creates – even though the base spell is Evocation magic (similar to Shadow Conjuration being an illusion spell, but the spells it creates are conjuration spells), the Target is how many people could be affected, and the d20 Roll is how the spell is administered (as well as determining how you and the target interact with the spell).

Element

This spell’s element. This truly only matters if the spell deals damage. Air deals slashing damage as the sharp wind cuts the skin. Water deals bludgeoning damage as it batters its foes. Earth pierces foes as rocky spikes jut out to stab with.

Range

Spell Range depends on the Target determined. Rays have a range of Close (25 ft. + 5 ft./2 levels), the 10 foot radius burst and the wall have a range of Medium (100 ft. + 10 ft./level), and the 20 foot radius spread has a range of Long (400 ft. + 40 ft./level).

If the spell is an attack roll, this is an attack roll against Touch AC and instead deals 1d8 points of damage per 2 caster levels you possess (to a maximum of 10d8 at 20th level).

If the spell is a caster level check, this functions as Dispel Magic, rolling a caster level check against the target(s).

If the spell is a concentration check, if the target(s) possess any ongoing spell effects currently affecting them (such as Shield or Mage Armor) you siphon one of the spell effects and it now is affecting you instead of them for its duration. If you don’t use a Spellcraft to identify what spells are currently affecting them, you instead take whichever is the highest level spell affecting them (if multiple exist of the same level, roll randomly to determine which is taken).

If the spell is a combat maneuver, choose a combat maneuver to perform with the spell. You use your caster level in place of your base attack bonus, and your casting attribute for the attribute added (in place of Strength or Dexterity). You add +1 to this check per 2 caster levels (to a maximum of a +10 bonus added to the check at 20th level).

If the spell is an initiative roll, you make an initiative check against the target(s) against their CMD. If you succeed against their CMD, they are considered flat-footed for 1 round + 1 round per 5 you beat their CMD. You add +1 to this check per caster level (to a maximum of a +20 bonus added to the check at 20th level).
